body: I've been looking into frequent but random freezes for 3 months now and found this issue after pinpointing my freeze cases to these conditions: - any Godot 4 Linux build, tested lots of Godot versions past 3 months - any Linux distro (tested Bazzite-nvidia, Bazzite-nvidia-open, Bazzite-gnome, Ubuntu X and Wayland sessions ) - any Nvidia driver, tested dozen versions over 3-6 months basically as far as the Bazzite repo lets me (I have RTX 2080 GPU) - Godot Wayland setting on or off - Freeze always happens on Forward+ and Mobile renderers (suggesting Vulkan issue ?) - Freeze will never happen on Compatibility renderer - The trigger seems to be rendering additional Godot windows on top of 3D viewport containing GPUParticles3D, AND mouse hovering over fields that will show tooltips on the additional Godot window - Tooltips from the main Godot window will not trigger freezing - Tooltips from additional Godot windows will not trigger freezing if no GPUParticles3D are being drawn in current main window Currently minimal steps to reproduce freeze for me: - Open 3D scene containing GPUParticles3D - Open a window like Signal window and mouseover tooltip while GPUParticles3D is animating in the background - While holding the mouseover, application will freeze in ~5 seconds, the additional window and / or tooltip will stay ghosting atop desktop environment if I alt-tab. Godot task will not recover and needs to be killed. EDIT: Tooltips from additional windows on top of Game view with GPUParticles3D do not trigger the freeze, only Editor 3D views are affected.

Wow, thank you @kheetor! I've also been trying to track down what was going on with these freezes for weeks. I don't think it's specifically limited to `GPUParticles3D`, though - I have seen it in a project without any particles. It does seem to require a 3D scene in the background. A `GPUParticles3D` node seems like it might be causing it to happen sooner, but it's hard to tell as it usually takes 10+ seconds for me in either case.

Not sure if it helps find the underlying cause, but debugging godot while I reproduce the freeze shows every thread in `__syscall_cancel_arch` being called from the NVidia driver.

[godot_gdb.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25139700/godot_gdb.log)

I have the same problem.
Turning on "single window mode" stops the editor from freezing for me as well.

I use Fedora 43, Geforce RTX 3080, Godot 4.6.1.

Same here. I am on Linux Aurora  (Fedora based) RX 9060 (16gb) Godot 4.6.1 (flatpak) 

Didn't have any issues until recently. Had a system update and suddenly couldn't add any nodes to the scene(s) anymore. The editor would freeze up.

Turning on Single window mode in Editor > Editor Settings did work.

So, after some testing I was able to trigger this consistently. 
The conditions are:
-  **3 or more** windows are opened at the same time (including main and tooltips)
- Changing focus of the window element

Some observations:
- Can happen regardless of the "prefer wayland" setting
- Can happen with Forward+ and Mobile renderers, but not Compatibility

How to reproduce (easiest):
_Obviously, single window mode needs to be disabled_
1. Make shader editor a floating window
2. Open "Add Node" window inside a visual shader (it will be the third window)
3. Hold Tab for 15-30 seconds (or just hover your mouse around the window elements)

Alternative (2 windows and a tooltip):
1. Open shader editor as embedded
2. Open "Add Node" window 
3. Hover your mouse over any category for a tooltip to appear 
4. Hold Tab for 15-30 seconds

It can happen with any similar setup of windows.

I use Arch+Hyprland with nvidia 580.126.18-2 drivers
Tested with Godot 4.7 dev-2 and 4.6.1

After 5 months of wasting time I fixed the issue by buying an AMD GPU. Also resolved system sleep hardlocks, monitor display mode registering quirks on wake, and random raytracing crashes. Everything just works and I no longer have to pick between making a 2D game and using Single Window Mode.

And I'm reading between the lines this is the intended fix. I hope people understand having your entire desktop freeze randomly when you're trying through fresh Linux installations, overwhelming majority of users will immediately fall back to Windows and/or Unity long before they begin to consider replacing their hardware.

It's fine to assume nobody uses 3D Godot on Linux NVIDIA drivers, but I don't see why Godot still couldn't let affected users know about the issue and be also transparent about the prioritization.

(According to Steam Hardware survey Feb 2026 85% of users have Nvidia GPU while 10% use AMD)

I've been having this exact issue since switching to Linux a few months ago. Never had this issue for the couple years I've used Godot 4 on Windows 10. 

When it happens, all Godot windows will become unresponsive while other apps running on my PC are fine. Minimizing and un-minimizing Godot will turn the windows black or completely transparent. Need to force quit to close Godot.

Originally encountered on Godot 4.5 when trying to export my game and navigating to the file export path, right-clicking and attempting to make a new folder. I realized it's only an issue when I have extra window elements open (like right-click menus and tooltips). Issue persists on 4.6.1 on a new project that only has one 3D scene with one Blender-imported model (both my projects have involved 3D), this time by right-clicking in the AnimationTree editor to add visual nodes.

Edit: 
Summary of my findings:
- Reproducible on Godot 4.5 and 4.6.1
- Fedora 43 KDE
- Did not occur on my same PC using Windows 10
- Nvidia GeForce 3080 (version 580.126.18)
- Tested official binary, native Fedora, and Flatpak
- Occurs regardless of Wayland or X11 (XWayland) - toggled Prefer Wayland and changing Flatpak settings
- Only on Forward+ and Mobile, not Compatibility
- Only occurs when Single Window Mode is not enabled

Steps to reproduce:
- Be on Linux and Nvidia GPU
- Pop out Script window
- Hover over FileSystem, right-click, Create New > Folder
- Hover over the second dropdown menu for a few seconds (5-10 seconds)
- Everything is permanently frozen, cannot close windows without force quitting

This issue has been fixed for me since updating my NVIDIA driver (now 595.45.04). Someone on Bluesky mentioned it was specifically fixed in version 590.x. I suggest others who have struggled with this to try updating their drivers! 

While I don't know the exact cause, several Vulkan-related highlights are listed here: https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/drivers/details/259313/

Edit: Seems like this is a duplicate of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/111931 !

I'm also experiencing this in Godot 4.6.1 on Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS with an Intel® Graphics (ADL GT2) card. It happens more than 50% of the time when I hover over a tooltip that's showing API information in the code editorp

Freezing on Ubuntu 26.04 with NVIDIA driver 580.142. 
Using single window configuration as workaround.

I **still frequently have this issue multiple times a day.**
Enabling `Single Window Mode` sucks because then I lose the embedded game view which is how I do most of my debugging. 

**I have not been able to figure out how to replicate, reproduce, or log the error to fix it.**

Edit: just saw the reproduction steps outline here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/114986#issuecomment-4123953954

Going to fresh compile 4.6.3 stable https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/35e80b3a8822a9df9be390814b62f44c0a9c69e8 and see if I can solve it.

**I may have found something!**

vkAcquireNextImageKHR is called with UINT64_MAX in RenderingDeviceDriverVulkan::swap_chain_acquire_framebuffer ([drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp:3653](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.6.3-stable/drivers/vulkan/rendering_device_driver_vulkan.cpp#L3653)). On NVIDIA + Wayland the nested wl_subsurface created by the game embedder reliably stalls this call, hanging the render thread and the whole editor.

My change is to swap the infinite wait for a finite timeout, skip the frame on timeout, and prefer MAILBOX over FIFO on NVIDIA. I'm going to do some testing locally and if it works I can submit a proper PR based on master, instead of branched off 4.6.3-stable. 

Here is a gist of the changes in a .patch you can apply and test yourself: https://gist.github.com/bearlikelion/9519e4aaa5807b84e6ca028819025ad9 (again, based on **4.6.3-stable**)

Is _anyone_ having this issue **without using the embedded game window?**

Confirming my previous patch **seems to have fixed this issue.** I have not had it reoccur in the last day of active game development. _But_ this is a systemic vendor specific change for Nvidia proprietary drivers on Wayland moving from FIFO -> MAILBOX. I'm only just getting into rendering C++ code so I would like someone else with experience with Godot's renderer to chime in before I create a proper PR to merge this. Some research threads: https://www.reddit.com/r/vulkan/comments/1fnh0v1/real_advantages_of_fifo_over_mailbox/ https://www.reddit.com/r/vulkan/comments/17jst1v/why_use_immediate_over_mailbox_in_vulkan/ https://zamundaaa.github.io/wayland/2021/12/14/about-gaming-on-wayland.html https://docs.vulkan.org/samples/latest/samples/performance/swapchain_images/README.html Googling: The editor _feels_ substantially more responsive with a higher frame rate, but I have not benchmarked a comparison. I have been busy focused on developing [SurfsUp](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3454830/SurfsUp/). @Calinou I'm not sure who to tag to review or provide feedback on this issue.

My patch also sets this as an optional toggle under `Project Settings/rendering/rendering_device/vulkan/nvidia_prefer_mailbox_present` I am going to toggle it _off_ to see if I can recreate the issue with the timeout patch on FIFO

Disabling Mailbox to revert back to FIFO and recreating the issue **causes significant delay/stutter** in the editor, but no longer freezes or goes unresponsive with an infinite timeout like it does without the patch.

I recall we tried to favor Mailbox V-Sync at some point, but there were issues on NVIDIA + X11 specifically.

Note that on Android, mailbox V-Sync is sometimes better supported than FIFO V-Sync on Vulkan. It's also the only way to uncap framerate past the refresh rate, as disabled V-Sync (immediate) is not supported at all on Android. Regardless, behavior remains highly vendor-specific and needs testing in real world scenarios.

As mentioned in https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/11583#issuecomment-2641272555, FIFO V-Sync support on Wayland is kind of a hack in Godot right now. Using Mailbox V-Sync might sidestep the issue, but won't fix the underlying problem.

Personally, I would prefer the editor to run with either immediate or mailbox V-Sync mode by default, since it lowers input lag by 2 frames (= 33.3 ms at 60 Hz) and tearing is usually not a problem in non-game applications. When paired with https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115548, the maximum framerate should be equivalent to FIFO V-Sync, so resource utilization should remain the same.

I've also ran into this issue and can reproduce on Linux Mint 22 with i7 first gen and EVA GTX 1050. I start a new scene, add an FBX object, do some adjustments. It will freeze when trying to close the project whether I save or not.

Hi people. For "prefer wayland" users on hyprland, jay, kwin, and mutter I have a workaround you can try: #121935 (you'll need to run the engine with `GODOT_WAYLAND_DISABLE_NATIVE_FIFO=1`)

The details are a bit complicated and also why I can't easily explain what's going on. For sure, I can say, that the embedded game freezing should not in any way affect the main window. They are completely separate processes and renderers. It could crash FWIW and the editor would be fine.

It probably won't fix all the reported cases here (given that lots of you are using XWayland and/or other compositors), but maybe it will alleviate the native wayland experience for some, while being less invasive than #121712 (since we do already have a mailbox workaround there, we just disabled it under the four compositors I mentioned)

Unfortunately the nvidia driver is very broken and it's not the first time it freezes with multiple windows. I remember it freezing my whole system during the 4.0 alpha xD
